description: Cross-platform compatibility test vectors for KnishIO Kotlin and JavaScript clients

base58_encoding.description: Base58 encoding/decoding test vectors for all character sets

molecular_hash.description: Molecular hash calculation test vectors. IMPORTANT: Value strings in atoms must be used VERBATIM — the molecular hash depends on exact string representation. The canonical format omits trailing '.0' for whole numbers (e.g., '-1000' not '-1000.0'). Some SDKs serialize with decimal points which produces a different hash.

wots_signature.description: WOTS+ signature generation and verification test vectors

mlkem768.description: ML-KEM768 (FIPS-203) cross-SDK vectors. keygen-from-seed is deterministic (byte-frozen); decapsulation+AES-256-GCM decrypt is deterministic (one captured encrypt sample frozen, since encapsulation is non-deterministic). Recipe: seed=generateSecret(secret,128)->64-byte d||z; ml_kem768.keygen; pubkey=raw-bytes Base64; encapsulate->32-byte shared secret used DIRECTLY as the AES-256-GCM key (no HKDF), 12-byte IV, 128-bit tag; envelope={cipherText, encryptedMessage:b64(IV||ct||tag)}.

mlkem1024.description: ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS-203) cross-SDK vectors. keygen-from-seed is deterministic (byte-frozen); decapsulation+AES-256-GCM decrypt is deterministic (one captured encrypt sample frozen, since encapsulation is non-deterministic). Recipe: seed=generateSecret(secret,128)->64-byte d||z; ml_kem1024.keygen; pubkey=raw-bytes Base64; encapsulate->32-byte shared secret used DIRECTLY as the AES-256-GCM key (no HKDF), 12-byte IV, 128-bit tag; envelope={cipherText, encryptedMessage:b64(IV||ct||tag)}.

legacyMlkem768AuthMolecule.description: A signed U+I auth molecule whose U-atom walletPubkey meta is an ML-KEM-768 public key (1184 raw bytes / 1580 base64 chars) — the shape a pre-bump 0.9.x client produced. ML-KEM-768 keygen from a given 64-byte seed is byte-unchanged across the 1024 migration (proven by the untouched vectors.mlkem768.keygen block, which all eight SDKs still reproduce byte-identically), and molecular hashing treats walletPubkey as an opaque meta string, so this molecule is bit-identical to one a pre-bump client would have produced from the same pinned inputs. Every SDK must validate it from a build whose default parameter set is ML-KEM-1024.

wotsSignedMetadataMolecule.description: Frozen WOTS+ signature of the eight-SDK self-test metaCreation molecule: seed TESTSEED, token USER, sourcePosition 0123456789abcdeffedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210, metaType TestMeta, metaId TESTMETA123, meta {name: 'Test Metadata', description: 'This is a test metadata for SDK testing.'}, remainder wallet at the self-tests' fixed position bbbb000000000000cccc111111111111dddd222222222222eeee333333333333, atom createdAt = 1700000000000 + 1000*index. Produced by KnishIO-Client-JS 1.2.0 on 2026-09-21; TypeScript, Python, PHP, Kotlin, Rust and C produced byte-identical otsFragments in the same run. An SDK that builds and signs this molecule MUST reproduce expectedOtsFragments exactly; an SDK verifier MUST accept `molecule`. Note that the molecule-level createdAt is the producing run's wall clock and is not covered by the molecular hash (only atoms are), so it is evidence of provenance, not an input to reproduce.

meta.value: This is a test metadata for SDK testing.

nacl.description: Classical NaCl crypto_box (X25519 scalarmult_base + XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox) parity vectors, captured from the reference tweetnacl and reproduced byte-for-byte by the BouncyCastle NaClBox (Kotlin) and every SDK's classical encryption path. Values are Base64 unless the key name ends in Hex. crypto_box + scalarMultBase are deterministic; the sealed-box sample uses a fixed ephemeral key so its blob is frozen for a decrypt oracle (live seal() uses a random ephemeral).

secret_storage_envelope.description: AES-GCM secret-storage envelope: the at-rest format shared by all eight SecretStorageProviders (C, C++, JS, TS, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Rust). The crypto core (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 x100000, 16-byte salt, 12-byte IV, AES-256-GCM with the tag appended to the ciphertext, standard padded base64, no AAD) was always identical across SDKs; the JSON FRAMING was not. Rust 0.9.5 emitted snake_case metadata keys and rejected this payload with 'missing field bundle_hash' before any crypto ran, while a Rust-written envelope deserialized in TS with every typed metadata field undefined. Metadata keys are camelCase - that is the contract. A consumer test must DECRYPT this frozen payload, not merely round-trip its own output: a round-trip passes in every SDK regardless of casing, which is why the divergence shipped. requiredMetadataKeys is a superset check; forbiddenMetadataKeys are the 0.9.5 snake_case forms and must never be emitted. Optional metadata keys are OMITTED when unset — never emitted as null (frozen 2026-09-11): Kotlin uses explicitNulls=false, Rust skip_serializing_if, TS/JS drop undefined. A consumer checking 'label' in metadata therefore reads the same answer regardless of the writing SDK. tests[1] is a frozen RECOVERY record (storageKey prefix knishio:recovery:, sealed under recoveryPassphrase, hardwareBacked always false): a consumer must seed ONLY that record, call recoverSecret(bundleHash, recoveryPassphrase, {passphrase}) and prove the re-enrolled primary at knishio:secret:<bundleHash> decrypts under {passphrase}. providerType is informational — TS/JS write webcrypto-aes-gcm, the other six write aes-gcm — and no SDK may reject a record on it.

kotlin.base58: Custom implementation with support for multiple character sets
kotlin.wots: Custom WOTS+ implementation with hash normalization

javascript.base58: Should use same character sets and encoding logic
javascript.wots: Must implement identical hash normalization algorithm
javascript.encryption: Should support same encryption modes and formats

setup: 1. Run this test vector generator in Kotlin to produce actual values
2. Use the generated test-vectors-generated.json file for validation
3. Run the JavaScript test suite with the same test vectors
continuous_validation: 1. Any changes to cryptographic functions should regenerate test vectors
2. Both platforms should run the same test vectors on each release
3. Failed compatibility tests should block releases until resolved
